questions.stem: What does the woman say she will do?
questions.stemZh: 女士说她将做什么?
questions.answerText: Sign the agreement if one small change is made to it.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: W: I have, indeed. And I wish to sign the agreement pending one small change to be made to the contract. 女：我确实同意了。而且我希望签署这份协议，前提是合同里做一处小改动。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 被问者的直接应答 + I wish to 表态。上一句男方问 Have you agreed to my last proposal?，女方紧接着应答 I have, indeed. And I wish to sign the agreement pending one small change，这句既是被问者的直接回应，又含 I wish to 的明确表态，正 是答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: I wish to sign the agreement ↔Sign the agreement I wish to do = 表示要做该动作 pending one small change to be made to the contract ↔if one small change is made to it pending = if，都是 "先改一处为条件"

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 A 借了男方话里的 my last proposal 拼成 Reply to the man's last proposal within a short time.，可她在 I have, indeed 里已经回复并表态要签，根本没说 "短时间内回复"， within a short time 是凭空加的。 借用原文：Have you agreed to my last proposal? C) 张冠李戴 C 的 Make a sponsorship deal for her client at the meeting. 用了录音里的 make a sponsorship deal for your clients，但那是男方反问 "你到底要不要做这笔交易"，并非女 方此刻 "我要做什么" 的回答；本题问的是她当下表态，答案是签约。 借用原文：Are you sure you want to make a sponsorship deal for your clients D) 原词陷阱 D 的 Give the man some good news regarding the contract. 盗了男方那句 please give me some good news，那是男方的请求 / 期待，女方并没说 "我要给你好消息"，她 说的是愿意签约。 借用原文：please give me some good news

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: M: I ask this, because, frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience. 男：我之所以这么问，是因为坦白说，我这边有些人快没耐心了。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 因果 because 后给出他对己方人员的真实描述。他用 because, frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience，because 引出对 "我这边的人" 的实情描述， frankly（坦白说）更是加重语气的强调信号，这句就是答案句。

analysis.text: B) 原词陷阱 B 的 time is running out 盗用了录音 running out of patience 里的 running out，却把 宾语偷换成 time。录音里耗尽的是耐心，不是时间，B 在 running out 后面动了手脚。 借用原文：running out of patience C) 答非所问 C 的 used to making alterations 取自录音 making alterations，但那是男方说双方 "这一 年来回改来改去" 的背景，不是在描述 "我方那些人现在什么状态"，答非所问。 借用原文：we've been through this for almost a year now, back and forth, making alterations D) 张冠李戴 D 的 concerned about the details 实际对应女方后面说的 We therefore comb through the fine details of all contracts，那是女方一边推敲细节，与男方所说 "我那边的人没耐 心" 是两拨人、两回事。 借用原文：We therefore comb through the fine details of all contracts

questions.stem: What reason does the woman give for the new deal to exclude the Middle East?
questions.stemZh: 女士给出了什么理由说明新协议要排除中东地区?
questions.answerText: To avoid any conflict of interest.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: W: Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would need to ensure that both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically. 女：因此，为了避免任何冲突，我们需要确保两个营销活动在地域上不重叠。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: in order to / therefore 双因果信号引出真目的。她先讲客户在中东另有营销意向，再用 Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would need to ensure that both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically，therefore 与 in order to 双双 标出这是给理由的句子，正是答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: in order to avoid any conflict ↔To avoid any conflict of interest. avoid any conflict 与选项几乎原义对应 both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically ↔conflict of interest 两活动地域不重叠 = 不产生利益冲突

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 A 的 To prevent geographical discrimination. 蹭了录音 overlap geographically 里的 geographically，造出 "地域歧视"。原文讲的是两个营销活动地域别重叠，与 "歧视" 毫不 相干，是借词造假。 借用原文：both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically B) 答非所问 B 的 To tap the food and beverage market. 用了录音 our food and beverage market，但那是男方在第12段说自家所属行业，与女方排除中东的理由无关；她的理由是 避免冲突，不是去开发某市场。 借用原文：So long as the product is very different from our food and beverage market D) 未提及 D 的 To reduce unfair competition. 听着像商务套话，但录音通篇没说要减少不公平竞 争，她讲的是避免客户形象在同一地域撞车的利益冲突，competition 一词原文压根没出 现。

questions.stem: What does the man say about the Middle East?
questions.stemZh: 男士关于中东地区说了什么?
questions.answerText: It is a negligible market for his company.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: M: The Middle East is a negligible market for us, but I still need to check this with a couple of departments. 男：中东对我们来说是个可以忽略的市场，不过我还是得跟几个部门核实一下。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 他对中东的直接评价句 + 形容词 negligible。他直说 The Middle East is a negligible market for us，主系表结构直接给出评价形容词 negligible，是对中东的正面定性句，正 是答案句；后半 but 起的只是补充程序，不改这句评价。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: a negligible market for us ↔a negligible market for his company for us = for his company，几乎原义

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 A 的 It is a potential market for food and beverage. 把中东说成 "有潜力"，与他原话 a negligible market（可忽略）正好相反；food and beverage 又是蹭了他讲己方行业的熟 词，双重误导。 借用原文：The Middle East is a negligible market for us B) 张冠李戴 B 的 It is very attractive for real estate developers. 借了女方说的中东 Real estate，但 那是女方客户在中东另有房地产营销意向，并非男方对中东市场的评价，张冠李戴。 借用原文：Real estate D) 偷换概念 D 的 It is very different from other markets. 盗用了 the product is very different from our food and beverage market 里的 very different，但原文说的是 "产品" 与食饮市场不 同，不是说 "中东市场" 与别的市场不同，主语被偷换。 借用原文：So long as the product is very different from our food and beverage market 1 M: Next, we have a special science-related news story. Paula Hancocks at the Denver Observatory. Paula, what is the big story over there? M: 接下来，我们有一条特别的科学相关新闻。Paula Hancocks 在 Denver 天文台。Paula，那边有什么 大新闻？ 2 W: Hi, John. Yes, all the astronomers on site here are very excited. In fact, space enthusiasts all across North America and the rest of the Northern Hemisphere will be congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night's sky. W: 嗨，John。是的，这里现场的所有天文学家都非常兴奋。事实上，整个北美和北半球其他地区的太空 爱好者今晚都会聚集在山顶上观看夜空。 3 M: Why? What's the big event? Is there an eclipse happening soon? M: 为什么？有什么大事件吗？是不是很快有日食发生？ 4 W: Tonight, the Earth will come into close proximity with the Oppenheimer comet. It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years. For this reason, it is expected that thousands of people will gaze up at the sky tonight in order to see this formidable object. W: 今晚，地球将与 Oppenheimer 彗星近距离接触。这是我们的星球在一百多年来与这种现象最接近的 一次。因此，预计今晚将有成千上万的人仰望天空，以观看这个令人敬畏的天体。 Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 5 M: How far away is this comet? Will people be able to see it with the naked eye? M: 这颗彗星有多远？人们能用肉眼看到它吗？ 6 W: The Oppenheimer comet will still be millions of miles away, on the edge of our galaxy. But nevertheless, this is a relatively close distance, close enough for people to observe in good detail through a telescope. People will only see a blur without one. However, that does not mean one needs professional equipment. Even the most ordinary of telescopes should be conducive for people to observe and wonder at this flying object. W: Oppenheimer 彗星仍将在数百万英里之外，在我们银河系的边缘。但尽管如此，这是一个相对较近 的距离，近到足以让人们通过望远镜详细观察。没有望远镜的话，人们只能看到一个模糊的影像。不过， 这并不意味着需要专业设备。即使是最普通的望远镜也应该足以让人们观察并惊叹于这个飞行的天体。 7 M: Many of our viewers will be wondering how they too can take part in this once-in-a-lifetime event. Where will this comet be in the sky? How can people find it? M: 我们的许多观众会想知道他们如何也能参与这个千载难逢的事件。这颗彗星会在天空的什么位置？人 们怎么找到它？ 8 W: The comet will be almost exactly due north, at 60 degrees above the equator. However, finding the comet is indeed very tricky. And scientists here have told me there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this. W: 这颗彗星几乎正好在正北方，在赤道上方 60 度。不过，找到这颗彗星确实非常棘手。这里的科学家 告诉我，有很多手机应用程序可以帮助实现这一点。 9 M: How fantastic! Thank you, Paula, for the information. M: 太棒了！谢谢你，Paula，提供这些信息。

questions.answerText: They are thrilled by a rare astronomic phenomenon.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Yes, all the astronomers on site here are very excited. 是的，在这里现场的所有天文学家都非常兴奋。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 被问者的直接应答。男士在 what is the big story over there? 抛出问题，女士开口第一句 all the astronomers on site here are very excited 就是直接应答，对话题的答案落在回答 方，这句即落点。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: all the astronomers on site here are very excited ↔ They are thrilled by a rare astronomic phenomenon. excited 同义改写为 thrilled

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 张冠李戴 录音 congregating on mountain tops 确实念到"山顶"，但那是"聚集去观星"，不是 celebrating a big event on mountain tops 的"在山顶庆祝"，且主语是北美各地爱好者， 非天文台的天文学家。 借用原文：congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night's sky C) 原词陷阱 开头 a special science-related news story 念到"科学相关"，C 项 enthusiastic about big science-related stories 直接搬这串词，但录音说的是天文学家"为这次天象兴奋"，不 是"热衷各种科学新闻故事"，把对一次具体天象的兴奋偷换成对科学故事的泛泛热衷。 借用原文：a special science-related news story D) 张冠李戴 录音 space enthusiasts all across North America 说的是"北美各地的爱好者要聚集"，D 项 joined by astronomers all across North America 把它改成"天文台的天文学家被北美 各地天文学家加入"，主语和事件都被偷换，原文没有这层意思。 借用原文：space enthusiasts all across North America and the rest of the Northern Hemisphere will be congregating

questions.stem: What do we learn from the conversation about the Oppenheimer comet?
questions.stemZh: 从对话中我们了解到关于Oppenheimer彗星的什么信息?
questions.answerText: It will come closest to Earth in more than one hundred years.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Tonight, the Earth will come into close proximity with the Oppenheimer comet. It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years. 今晚，地球将与奥本海默彗星近距离接近。这是一百多年来我们的星球离这样一种天象最近 的一次。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 正面定性句 + 时间数字。女士直接给彗星定性 It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years，"closest…in over 100 years" 把"距离最 近"和"百年"绑在一起，是带数字的定性句，正是答案落点。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years ↔ It will come closest to Earth in more than one hundred years. 主被动对调 + 数字同义

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 录音后文 this formidable object 确有 "formidable"，A 项 the most formidable of its kind in over a century 便把"百年"嫁接到"最厉害"上；但原文里"百年"修饰的是"距离最 近"，从没说它是百年来"最厉害"的，是把数字按到了错的形容词上。 借用原文：in order to see this formidable object C) 过度推断 eclipse many other such events in human history 借"eclipse"（此处作动词"使相形见 绌"）和前文 Is there an eclipse happening soon? 的"日食"玩文字游戏，原文从没说这颗 彗星"使人类历史上其他天象相形见绌"，属凭空拔高。 借用原文：Is there an eclipse happening soon? D) 原词陷阱 seen most clearly from Denver's mountain tops 把前文 the Denver Observatory 的"丹佛"和 mountain tops 的"山顶"拼到一起，但原文只说爱好者会聚到山顶观星，从没 说"从丹佛的山顶看得最清楚"，是把零散原词攒成一句没说过的话。 借用原文：congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night's sky

questions.stem: What does the woman say people will only see in the sky without a telescope?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士说人们在没有望远镜的情况下在天空中只能看到什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: People will only see a blur without one. 没有望远镜的话，人们只会看到模糊的一团。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 条件 without one + only 直陈。这句用 without one（one 指代上文 telescope）锁 定"不用望远镜"的前提，再用 only see a blur 直说看到什么，前提和结果都摆明，是答 案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: People will only see a blur without one ↔blur. 原句直取，前提一致

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 未提及 录音通篇没说不用望远镜会看到"星星"，Stars. 是凭"看星空"的常识脑补出来的，原文只说 看到"一团模糊"。 C) 原词陷阱 on the edge of our galaxy 念到"星系边缘"，但那是说彗星"所在的位置"，不是"不用望远 镜看到的东西"，C 项 The edge of our galaxy. 把"它在哪"偷换成"看到什么"。 借用原文：The Oppenheimer comet will still be millions of miles away, on the edge of our galaxy D) 与原文相反 wonder at this flying object 念到 "flying object"，但那是"用普通望远镜能观赏到的彗 星"，D 项 An ordinary flying object. 把它挪到"不用望远镜"的前提下——条件正好反了， 不用望远镜只见模糊团，看不清是个"飞行物"。 借用原文：Even the most ordinary of telescopes should be conducive for people to observe and wonder at this flying object

options.label: B

questions.stem: What do scientists at the Denver Observatory advise amateurs do to facilitate their observation?
questions.stemZh: 丹佛天文台的科学家们建议业余爱好者做什么来便于他们的观测?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: And scientists here have told me there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this. 这里的科学家告诉我，有很多手机应用程序可以帮上这个忙。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 建议句 + 与题干同词 facilitate。女士转述科学家的建议 there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this，"scientists…told me"对应题干的"scientists advise"，"facilitate"与题干 facilitate their observation 同词，是答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this ↔Make use of phone apps. 存在句 祈使建议

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 录音 that does not mean one needs professional equipment 明确说"并不需要专业设 备"，A 项 Use professional equipment. 直接搬这串原词却把否定改成肯定，意思正好反 了。 借用原文：that does not mean one needs professional equipment B) 原词陷阱 录音 congregating on mountain tops 念到"山顶"，B 项 Climb to the nearby heights. （爬到附近高处）借此设套，但那是说爱好者去哪儿聚集，不是科学家"为方便观测给的建 议"，问的根本不是同一件事。 借用原文：will be congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night's sky C) 原词陷阱 录音 The comet will be almost exactly due north 念到"正北"，那是在说彗星"在天上的 位置"，C 项 Fix their eyes due north. 把"它在正北方"偷换成"建议人们眼睛盯着正北"，而 科学家给的方便观测的办法是用 app，不是"盯着北方"。 借用原文：The comet will be almost exactly due north, at 60 degrees above the equator Section B 1 Dietary guidelines form the basis for nutrition advice and regulations around the world. While there is strong scientific consensus around most existing guidelines, one question has recently stirred debate: should consumers be warned to avoid ultra-processed foods? 膳食指南构成了全球营养建议和法规的基础。尽管现有指南大多已达成强有力的科学共识,但最近有一个问 题引发了争论:是否应该警告消费者避免超加工食品? 2 Two papers published today in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition outline the case for and against using the concept of ultra-processed foods to help inform dietary guidelines beyond conventional food classification systems. The authors, Carlos Monteiro of the University of São Paulo and Arne Astrup of Novo Nordisk Foundation, will discuss the issue in a live virtual debate August 14th during NUTRITION 2024 LIVE ONLINE. 今天发表在《美国临床营养学杂志》上的两篇论文概述了赞成和反对使用超加工食品概念来帮助指导膳 食指南超越传统食品分类系统的理由。作者Carlos Monteiro来自圣保罗大学,Arne Astrup来自Novo Nordisk基金会,他们将在8月14日NUTRITION 2024 LIVE ONLINE期间的现场虚拟辩论中讨论这个 问题。 3 The debate centers around a system developed by Monteiro and colleagues that classifies foods by their degree of industrial processing, ranging from unprocessed to ultra-processed. The system defines Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard. ultra-processed foods as those made using sequences of processes that extract substances from foods and alter them with chemicals in order to formulate the final product. Ultra-processed foods are characteristically designed to be cheap, tasty, and convenient; examples include soft drinks and candy, packaged snacks and pastries, ready-to-heat products, and reconstituted meat products. 这场辩论围绕着Monteiro及其同事开发的一个系统展开,该系统按工业加工程度对食品进行分类,从未加工 到超加工不等。该系统将超加工食品定义为使用一系列工艺从食品中提取物质并用化学物质改变它们以配 制最终产品的食品。超加工食品的特点是被设计得廉价、美味和方便;例子包括软饮料和糖果、包装零食和 糕点、即热产品以及重组肉制品。 4 Studies have linked consumption of ultra-processed foods—which are packed high in salt, sugar, and fat—with weight gain and an increased risk of chronic diseases, even after adjusting for the amount of salt, sugar, and fat in the diet. analysis.text: A) 未提及 A 说创造力 key to a company's survival（对公司生存至关重要），虽然录音提到 Mayer 曾是 Google 的副总裁，但她写的话里根本没提公司生存，A 凭 Google 这一职务背景臆造 出公司话题，属未提及。 B) 张冠李戴 B 说 It shapes and focuses problems.，这句确实摘自 Mayer 的话 Constraints shape and focus problems，但原文该动作的主语是 Constraints（约束）不是 creativity，题干 问的是关于 creativity 的内容，B 把约束做的事安到了创造力头上，主语张冠李戴。 借用原文：Constraints shape and focus problems C) 原词陷阱 C 说创造力 essential to meeting challenges（对应对挑战至关重要），录音里 challenges 一词出自 provide clear challenges to overcome，说的是约束提供需克服的 挑战，而非创造力对应对挑战必不可少，C 盗用 challenges 偷换了逻辑关系。 借用原文：provide clear challenges to overcome Section C 1 Different people use different strategies for managing conflicts. These strategies are learned in childhood. Usually, we are not aware of how we act in conflict situations. We just do whatever seems to come naturally. But we do have a personal strategy, and because it is learned, we can always change it by learning new and more effective ways of managing conflicts. When you get involved in a conflict, there are two major concerns you have to take into account: achieving your personal goals and keeping a good relationship with the other person. How important your personal goals are and how important the relationship is to you affect how you act in a conflict. Given these two concerns, five styles of managing conflicts can be identified. 不同的人使用不同的策略来管理冲突。这些策略是在童年时期学会的。通常,我们并不知道自己在冲突情境 中是如何行事的。我们只是做任何看似自然而然的事情。但我们确实有个人策略,而且因为它是习得的,我 们总是可以通过学习新的、更有效的冲突管理方式来改变它。当你卷入冲突时,你必须考虑两个主要关切: 实现你的个人目标和与他人保持良好关系。你的个人目标有多重要以及这段关系对你有多重要,会影响你在 冲突中的行为方式。基于这两个关切,可以识别出五种冲突管理风格。 2 The turtle. Turtles withdraw into their shells to avoid conflicts. They give up their personal goals and relationships. They believe it is easier to withdraw from a conflict than to face it. 海龟型。海龟缩进壳里以避免冲突。他们放弃个人目标和关系。他们认为退出冲突比面对冲突更容易。 Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard. 3 The shark. Sharks try to overpower opponents by forcing them to accept their solution to the conflict. They seek to achieve their goals at all costs. Sharks assume that conflicts are settled by one person winning and one person losing. Winning gives sharks a sense of pride and achievement. Losing gives them a sense of weakness, inadequacy, and failure. 鲨鱼型。鲨鱼试图通过强迫对手接受他们对冲突的解决方案来压倒对手。他们不惜一切代价寻求实现自己 的目标。鲨鱼认为冲突是通过一方获胜、一方失败来解决的。获胜给鲨鱼带来自豪感和成就感。失败则让 他们感到软弱、无能和失败。 4 The teddy bear. Teddy bears want to be accepted and liked by other people. They think that conflict should be avoided in favor of harmony, and believe that conflicts cannot be discussed without damaging relationships. They give up their goals to preserve the relationship. 泰迪熊型。泰迪熊希望被他人接受和喜欢。他们认为应该避免冲突以维护和谐,并相信冲突无法在不损害关 系的情况下讨论。他们为了保持关系而放弃自己的目标。 5 The fox. Foxes are moderately concerned with their own goals and about their relationships with other people. They give up part of their goals and persuade the other person in a conflict to give up part of his goals. They seek a solution to conflicts where both sides gain something. 狐狸型。狐狸对自己的目标和与他人的关系都适度关注。他们放弃部分目标,并说服冲突中的对方也放弃部 分目标。他们寻求让双方都有所收获的冲突解决方案。 6 The owl. Owls view conflicts as problems to be solved. They see conflicts as improving relationships by reducing tension between two people. They try to begin a discussion that identifies the conflict as a problem. By seeking solutions that satisfy both themselves and the other person, owls maintain the relationship. Owls are not satisfied until a solution is found that achieves their own goals and the other person's goals, and they are not satisfied until the tensions and negative feelings have been fully resolved. 猫头鹰型。猫头鹰将冲突视为需要解决的问题。他们认为冲突通过减少两人之间的紧张关系来改善关系。 他们试图发起讨论,将冲突确定为一个问题。通过寻求既满足自己又满足对方的解决方案,猫头鹰维持了关 系。猫头鹰只有在找到既实现自己目标又实现对方目标的解决方案时才会满意,只有在紧张和负面情绪得到 完全化解时才会满意。

analysis.text: Sir Jim Smith, Director of Science at Wellcome, said, "Try as I might, I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project." Wellcome 科学总监 Jim Smith 爵士说："无论我怎么想，都想不出还有比这更激动人心、 更切题、更及时、更具国际启发性的项目。"

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 评价语气：I can't think of a more… 是变相最高级。答案句靠 I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project 这 个"想不出更…的"否定结构锁定——"想不出比它更…的"等于"它是最…的"，是说话人对项目 的最高评价。

analysis.text: I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project ↔It is the most exciting, most relevant, most timely and most internationally inspirational. "想不出更…的"="最…的"，比较级转最高级

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 It dwarfs all other efforts to conserve, protect and restore biodiversity on earth. 蹭了 录音 conserve as well as protect and restore biodiversity 的原词，但说"它使其它一切 保护努力相形见绌"是录音没有的比较，且这是 Jim Smith 的评价题，A 拼的是别处第 3 段 的料，张冠李戴。 借用原文：bolster efforts to conserve as well as protect and restore biodiversity B) 答非所问 It is costly to get started and requires the joint efforts of thousands of scientists. 蹭 了录音 cost £100 million 与众多科学家协作的料，但这是讲项目的成本与规模，是客观事 实，不是 Jim Smith"如何形容/评价"项目，答非所问。 借用原文：it is expected to take 10 years and cost £100 million C) 过度推断 It can help to bring back the large numbers of plants and animals that have gone extinct. 用了录音常出现的"动植物灭绝"原词，但录音只说项目能助保护、记录生命，从没 说能"把已灭绝物种带回来"，明显过度推断。 借用原文：we desperately need to catalogue life on our fragile planet now 1 John Donne, the English poet, wrote in the 17th century, "No man is an island, entire of itself; every man is a piece of the continent, a part of the main." Now, a British academic has claimed that human individuality is indeed just an illusion, because societies are far more interconnected at a mental, physical, and cultural level than people realise. In his new book, The Self Delusion, Professor Tom Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard. Oliver, a researcher in the Ecology and Evolution group at the University of Reading, argues there is no such thing as "self", and not even our bodies are truly "us". 17世纪英国诗人约翰·多恩写道："没有人是一座孤岛，可以自全；每个人都是大陆的一片，是整体的一部 分。"现在,一位英国学者声称,人类的个体性确实只是一种幻觉,因为社会在心理、生理和文化层面的相互联 系远比人们意识到的要紧密得多。雷丁大学生态与进化研究小组的研究员汤姆·奥利弗教授在他的新书《自 我的错觉》中指出,不存在所谓的"自我",甚至连我们的身体也不是真正的"我们"。 2 Just as Copernicus realised the Earth is not the centre of the universe, Professor Oliver said society urgently needs a Copernican-like revolution to understand people are not detached beings but rather part of one connected identity. "A significant milestone in the cultural evolution of human minds was the acceptance that the Earth is not the centre of the universe, the so-called Copernican Revolution," he writes. "However, we have one more big myth to dispose of: that we exist as independent selves at the centre of a subjective universe. You may feel as if you are an independent individual, acting autonomously in the world; that you have an unchanging inner self that persists throughout your lifetime, acting as a central anchor-point with the world changing around you. This is the illusion I seek to tackle. We are intimately connected to the world around us." 正如哥白尼意识到地球不是宇宙的中心一样,奥利弗教授表示,社会迫切需要一场类似哥白尼式的革命,以理 解人们不是独立的存在,而是一个相互联系的整体的一部分。他写道:"人类思维文化演变中的一个重要里程 碑是接受地球不是宇宙的中心,即所谓的哥白尼革命。然而,我们还有一个重大的神话需要破除:我们作为独 立的自我存在于主观宇宙的中心。你可能觉得自己是一个独立的个体,在世界上自主行动;你有一个贯穿一 生的不变的内在自我,作为一个中心锚点,而世界在你周围变化。这就是我试图揭穿的幻觉。我们与周围的 世界紧密相连。" 3 Professor Oliver argues there are around 37 trillion cells in the body but most have a lifespan of just a few days or weeks, so the material "us" is constantly changing. In fact, there is no part of your body that has existed for more than 10 years. "Since our bodies are essentially made anew every few weeks, the material in them alone is clearly insufficient to explain the persistent thread of an identity." 奥利弗教授认为,人体内大约有37万亿个细胞,但大多数细胞的寿命只有几天或几周,因此物质层面的"我 们"在不断变化。事实上,你身体的任何部分都不曾存在超过10年。"由于我们的身体基本上每隔几周就会重 新生成,仅凭其中的物质显然不足以解释身份认同的持续性线索。" 4 Professor Oliver claims that individualism is actually bad for society, and only by realising we are part of a bigger entity can we solve pressing environmental and societal problems. Through selfish over- consumption we are destroying the natural world and using non-renewable resources at an accelerating rate. "We are at a critical crossroads as a species where we must rapidly reform our mindsets and behaviour to act in less selfish ways," he said. "So let's open our eyes to the hidden connections all around us." 奥利弗教授声称,个人主义实际上对社会有害,只有认识到我们是一个更大整体的一部分,我们才能解决紧迫 的环境和社会问题。通过自私的过度消费,我们正在破坏自然世界,并以越来越快的速度使用不可再生资 源。他说:"作为一个物种,我们正处于一个关键的十字路口,必须迅速改革我们的思维方式和行为,以更少自 私的方式行事。所以让我们睁开眼睛,看到我们周围隐藏的联系。"

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Now, a British academic has claimed that human individuality is indeed just an illusion, because societies are far more interconnected at a mental, physical, and cultural level than people realise. 如今，一位英国学者声称，人的个体独立性其实只是一种幻觉，因为社会在心理、生理和文 化层面上的相互联系远比人们意识到的紧密。

analysis.text: 原句直陈定性。答案句直接用 human individuality is indeed just an illusion 把某概念点 定为"幻觉"，is just an illusion 这种判定句就是信号，听到"X 其实只是个幻觉"就锁定 X。

questions.answerText: It is a delusion to be disposed of.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: However, we have one more big myth to dispose of: that we exist as independent selves at the centre of a subjective universe. 然而，我们还有一个大迷思需要破除：即我们以为自己是独立的自我、处在一个主观宇宙的 中心。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 转折However后是真意。句首 However 转折之后才是讲者真正要表达的态度，他把那个想 法称为 one more big myth to dispose of（又一个要破除的迷思），处置动词 dispose of 直接给出否定态度。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: one more big myth to dispose of ↔a delusion to be disposed of myth=delusion同义替换

analysis.text: D) 原词陷阱 rooted in the mindset of the 17th century 盗用了录音开头 wrote in the 17th century 的时间词，但 17 世纪说的是 John Donne 写诗的年代，讲者从未说那个"独立自我"的想法 植根于 17 世纪心态，属原词陷阱。 借用原文：wrote in the 17th century C) 张冠李戴 a myth spread by John Donne's poem 把"迷思"归因到 John Donne 的诗，盗用了开头 出现的 John Donne，但讲者引 Donne 的诗恰恰是支持"人互相连接"，并非说这首诗散布 了迷思，属张冠李戴。 借用原文：every man is a piece of the continent, a part of the main B) 未提及 prevalent even among academics（连学者中都很普遍）原文从未提及，讲者只说这是普 遍的 illusion，没有专门强调"在学者中尤其普遍"，属未提及。

questions.stemZh: 为什么Tom Oliver教授声称物质层面的"我们"在不断变化?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Professor Oliver argues there are around 37 trillion cells in the body but most have a lifespan of just a few days or weeks, so the material "us" is constantly changing. 奥利弗教授指出，人体内约有37万亿个细胞，但大多数细胞的寿命只有几天或几周，因此物 质意义上的"我们"在不断变化。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 因果so前是原因。句中 so the material "us" is constantly changing 的 so 是结果标志， so 之前的 most have a lifespan of just a few days or weeks 就是讲者给出的原因，正是 Why 题要找的依据句。

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 原词陷阱 ample scientific evidence at the University of Reading 盗用了录音第一段介绍学者时的 the University of Reading，但那只是说明他的任职单位，原文从未说他在该校获得了大量 科学证据，属原词陷阱。 借用原文：Professor Tom Oliver, a researcher in the Ecology and Evolution group at the University of Reading A) 答非所问 He believes in Copernican philosophical doctrines about the universe. 又借 Copernican 一词，但本题问的是"物质之我为何在变"，答案是细胞寿命，与哥白尼无关， 属答非所问。 借用原文：Just as Copernicus realised the Earth is not the centre of the universe C) 偷换概念 He has found that our inner self and material self are interconnected. 听上去与全 篇"互相连接"主旨呼应，但原文并未以"内在自我与物质自我相连"来解释物质之我为何变 化，是偷换概念、答非所问。 借用原文：We are intimately connected to the world around us.

analysis.text: D) 未提及 By making joint efforts resolutely and persistently（坚定持久地共同努力）听上去正确 且积极，但原文给的办法是"意识到自己属于更大整体"，并未说靠"坚定持久的共同努力"， 属未提及的正确话陷阱。 B) 偷换概念 By realising that we all can do our own bit in such endeavours（意识到人人能尽一份 力）借了 realising 一词，但原文 realising 后接的是"我们是更大整体的一部分"，不是"人 人能尽一份力"，属偷换概念。 借用原文：only by realising we are part of a bigger entity A) 未提及 By coming to see how disruptive such problems have got to be（认清这些问题有多具 破坏性）原文并未把"看清问题严重"作为解决之道，讲者给的解法是意识到自己属于更大整 体，属未提及。 W: Thank you for meeting with me, Stephen, at such short notice. 第1段，第1句 本句涵盖谓语、宾语、原因状语、时间状语四种成分，成分种类较丰富；祈使句的谓语识别、介词 短语作状语的判定均为基础但重要的练习点，适合巩固基本句型；但缺少主语、定语、宾补等成 分，覆盖面有限。 I ask this, because, frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience. 第4段，第3句 "主句 + because 引导的原因状语从句" 是考试中极为常见的复合句结构。插入语的使用也是真题中 的常见现象。动词短语 "run out of" 和现在进行时的搭配在实际语境中频繁出现。整体句式具有较 强的典型性和迁移价值。 Those offers, should they materialize, would exclusively employ my client's image in the Middle East only. 第9段，第2句 本句包含主语、谓语、宾语、地点状语、程度状语等多种成分，且条件从句插入主句造成主谓分 离，是练习识别主干、排除干扰成分的优质材料。倒装结构和情态动词搭配也是值得练习的易 错点。 Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would need to ensure that both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically. 第9段，第3句 本句体现 "情态动词 + 及物动词 + 宾语从句" 和 "目的状语前置" 两种常见句式,均为四六级和考 研阅读中的高频结构。宾语从句的识别和目的状语的理解都是典型考点,具有较强的代表性和迁移 价值。 So long as the product is very different from our food and beverage market, there should be no conflict of interest. 第12段，第2句 本句使用 "So long as" 引导条件状语从句，这是四六级和考研阅读中常见的复杂句式之一。"there should be" 结构也是典型的书面表达方式，学习者掌握后可以迁移到类似的条件或假设情境中。 Nevertheless, I will have to run this through my people. 第12段，第3句 本句是标准的简单句结构（主谓宾加状语），这种句型在四六级和考研阅读中极为常见。"will have to" 表示将来义务的用法也是高频结构，具有一定代表性。但由于缺少从句、并列、特殊句式 等更复杂的常考结构，作为典型性练习句的价值处于中等水平——掌握后可复用，但覆盖的句式变 化不够丰富。 They are used to making alterations. 第2题，C "be used to doing" 是四六级和考研阅读中常见的固定搭配，本句结构简洁典型，掌握后可直接迁 移到其他包含该短语的句子，实用性强。 It is very different from other markets. 第4题，D 主系表结构是英语基本句型之一，高频出现，但本句过于简单，缺少考试中常见的修饰层次或从句 嵌套，作为典型例句代表性一般。 For this reason, it is expected that thousands of people will gaze up at the sky tonight in order to see this formidable object. 第4段，第3句 形式主语 it + be + 过去分词 + that 从句是四六级和考研阅读中的高频句式，常用于表达观点、预 of”这类固定搭配在建议类写作和说明文里相当常见，具备一定的代表性，但 结构本身较为简单，作为典型考试句式的复杂度不高。 The system defines ultra-processed foods as those made using sequences of processes that extract substances from foods and alter them with analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Supervisors also play a critical role. P1 It is irrefutable that employees know the difference between right and wrong. So why don't more employees intervene when they see someone exhibiting at-risk behavior in the workplace?

P2 There are a number of factors that influence whether people intervene. First, they need to be able to see a risky situation beginning to unfold. Second, the company's culture needs to make them feel safe to speak up. And third, they need to have the communication skills to say something effectively.

P3 This is not strictly a workplace problem; it's a growing problem off the job too. Every day people witness things on the street and choose to stand idly by. This is known as the bystander effect— the more people who witness an event, the less likely anyone in that group is to help the victim. The psychology behind this is called diffusion of responsibility. Basically, the larger the crowd, the more people assume that someone else will take care of it—meaning no one effectively intervenes or acts in a moment of need. 

P4 This crowd mentality is strong enough for people to evade their known responsibilities. But it's not only frontline workers who don't make safety interventions in the workplace. There are also instances where supervisors do not intervene either.

P5 When a group of employees sees unsafe behavior not being addressed at a leadership level it creates the precedent that this is how these situations should be addressed, thus defining the safety culture for everyone.

P6 Despite the fact that workers are encouraged to intervene when they observe unsafe operations, this happens less than half of the time. Fear is the ultimate factor in not intervening. There is a fear of penalty, a fear that they'll have to do more work if they intervene. Unsuccessful attempts in the past are another strong contributing factor to why people don't intervene—they tend to prefer to defer that action to someone else for all future situations.

P7 On many worksites, competent workers must be appointed. Part of their job is to intervene when workers perform a task without the proper equipment or if the conditions are unsafe. Competent workers are also required to stop work from continuing when there's a danger.

P8 Supervisors also play a critical role. Even if a competent person isn't required, supervisors need a broad set of skills to not only identify and alleviate workplace hazards but also build a safety climate within their team that supports intervening and open communication among them.

P9 Beyond competent workers and supervisors, it's important to educate everyone within the organization that they are obliged to intervene if they witness a possible unsafe act, whether you're a designated competent person, a supervisor or a frontline worker.

P1 The term "environmentalist" can mean different things. It used to refer to people trying to protect wildlife and natural ecosystems. In the 21st century, the term has evolved to capture the need to combat human-made climate change.

P2 The distinction between these two strands of environmentalism is the cause of a split within the scientific community about nuclear energy.

P3 On one side are purists who believe nuclear power isn't worth the risk and the exclusive solution to the climate crisis is renewable energy. The opposing side agrees that renewables are crucial, but says society needs an amount of power available to meet consumers' basic demands when the sun isn't shining and the wind isn't blowing. Nuclear energy, being far cleaner than oil, gas and coal, is a natural option, especially where hydroelectric capacity is limited. 

P4 Leon Clarke, who helped author reports for the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, isn't an uncritical supporter of nuclear energy, but says it's a valuable option to have if we're serious about reaching carbon neutrality.

P5 "Core to all of this is the degree to which you think we can actually meet climate goals with 100% renewables," he said. "If you don't believe we can do it, and you care about the climate, you are forced to think about something like nuclear."

P6 The achievability of universal 100% renewability is similarly contentious. Cities such as Burlington, Vermont, have been "100% renewable" for years. But these cities often have small populations, occasionally still rely on fossil fuel energy and have significant renewable resources at their immediate disposal. Meanwhile, countries that manage to run off renewables typically do so thanks to extraordinary hydroelectric capabilities.

P7 Germany stands as the best case study for a large, industrialized country pushing into green energy. Chancellor Angela Merkel in 2011 announced Energiewende, an energy transition that would phase out nuclear and coal while phasing in renewables. Wind and solar power generation has increased over 400% since 2010, and renewables provided 46% of the country's electricity in 2019.

P8 But progress has halted in recent years. The instability of renewables doesn't just mean energy is often not produced at night, but also that solar and wind can overwhelm the grid during the day, forcing utilities to pay customers to use their electricity. Lagging grid infrastructure struggles to transport this overabundance of green energy from Germany's north to its industrial south, meaning many factories still run on coal and gas. The political limit has also been reached in some places, with citizens meeting the construction of new wind turbines with loud protests.

P9 The result is that Germany's greenhouse gas emissions have fallen by around 11.5% since 2010 —slower than the EU average of 13.5%.

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 主干：习俗 has a long history（主语策略：原句主语） 本句信息多，但可立的核心主干是 中国的传统婚礼习俗历史悠久：主语 China's traditional wedding customs，谓语用 have a long history。后半 逐渐形成了一套完整的婚礼仪式 另起一 个分句，主语承前仍是这些习俗、谓语 took shape / a complete set ... took shape，有些一直沿 用至今 再起一个以 some of which 引导的分句。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 三动作分配到并列句与定语从句 本句含三个动作：历史悠久 / 形成仪式 / 沿用至今。处理为：主干 ...customs have a long history；从周朝开始就逐渐形成了一套完整的婚礼仪式 用 and a complete set of wedding ceremonies took shape ... starting from the Zhou Dynasty，“从周朝开始”降级为 starting from / as early as the Zhou Dynasty 作状语；有些一直沿用至今 降级为 some of which have been followed / passed down to this day 的定语从句，挂在 ceremonies 上，避免再起一个光 秃秃的短句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 “形成了一套仪式”是历史上已完成的动作，回指全篇基调虽以现在时为主，但此处叙述过去起源故 偏离为一般过去时 took shape；有些一直沿用至今 强调从过去延续到现在，用现在完成时 have been followed to this day。 单复数 “习俗”非单一项，customs 用复数；“一套完整的婚礼仪式”用 a complete set of wedding ceremonies，set 单数加 a，ceremonies 复数。 语态 “有些一直沿用至今”的逻辑主语是“被人们沿用”，用被动 have been followed / handed down， 比硬找主语更自然。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: China's traditional wedding customs have a long history. A complete set of wedding ceremonies gradually took shape as early as the Zhou Dynasty, some of which have been followed to this day. 2. 如今的中式婚礼习俗已有很大变化，但婚礼庆典仍然十分隆重。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 两分句各立主干，由 but 连接（主语策略：原句主语） 本句是“变化 + 但隆重”的转折结构。前半 如今的中式婚礼习俗已有很大变化 主语 today's Chinese wedding customs，谓语 have changed greatly；后半 婚礼庆典仍然十分隆重 主语 the wedding celebration，谓语用系表 is still grand / ceremonious。两个主干由转折连词 but 连接。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 结构本就简单，无需大改 本句是典型的“A but B”并列转折，前后各是简单句，不需要再降级成从句；只需选准转折连词 but，并把“很大变化”处理成 have changed greatly、“仍然十分隆重”处理成 remains / is still very grand 即可。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 “已有很大变化”强调到现在为止已经发生的变化，用现在完成时 have changed；后半“仍然十分隆 重”讲现在的状态，回指全篇基调用一般现在时 is / remains。 单复数与主谓一致 前半主语 customs 复数，谓语 have changed；后半主语 the wedding celebration 单数，谓语 is/remains，两处主谓数要分别对齐。 用词 “隆重”宜用 grand / ceremonious / solemn and grand，不要误用 lively（那是“热闹”）或 luxurious（奢华），程度词“十分”用 very / quite。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Today's Chinese wedding customs have changed greatly, but the wedding celebration remains very grand. 3. 婚礼场地经过精心装饰，以象征喜庆 (jubilance) 的红色为主色调，摆放着许多祝愿新人幸福 的物件。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 主干：场地 is decorated（主语策略：转被动） 本句围绕“婚礼场地”展开三个动作，主语统一锁定 the wedding venue。核心主干取 婚礼场地经 过精心装饰，“场地被装饰”是被动关系，故 the wedding venue is elaborately decorated 作主 干；以……红色为主色调 与 摆放着许多……物件 作为对场地的进一步描述降级安放。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 两个描述降级为介词短语与定语从句 以象征喜庆 (jubilance) 的红色为主色调 降级为介词短语 with red, the color symbolizing jubilance, as the main tone 作伴随状语；摆放着许多祝愿新人幸福的物件 用 where many objects ... are placed 的定语从句、或 with many objects ... 的伴随结构挂到 venue 上；其中“祝 愿新人幸福的”再用 wishing the couple happiness 的现在分词作后置定语修饰 objects。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态与语态 讲现在场地的惯常布置，回指全篇基调用一般现在时；“经过装饰”“被摆放”均为被动，用 is decorated、are placed。 单复数 “许多物件”是 many objects，复数；谓语 are placed 随之用复数。 用词与括注 “喜庆”沿用原文括注 jubilance；“主色调”用 main tone / dominant color；“祝愿……幸福”用 wishing the couple happiness 或 expressing good wishes for the couple，不要直译成 bless （含宗教色彩）。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The wedding venue is elaborately decorated, with red—the color symbolizing jubilance—as the main tone, and many objects wishing the couple happiness are placed around it. 4. 在婚礼上，新人要拜天地 (bow to Heaven and Earth)、拜父母和相互对拜，然后设宴招待宾 客，并向宾客敬酒致谢。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 主干：新人 bow ... then hold a banquet（主语策略：原句主语） 本句主语明确为“新人”the couple，是一连串动作的发出者。新人要拜天地 (bow to Heaven and Earth)、拜父母和相互对拜 是第一组并列谓语 bow to Heaven and Earth, to their parents and to each other；然后设宴招待宾客 是 then 引出的下一个谓语 hold a banquet to entertain the guests；并向宾客敬酒致谢 再并列一个谓语 propose toasts to thank them。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 目的动作降级为不定式 设宴招待宾客 中“招待宾客”是“设宴”的目的，降级为不定式 to entertain the guests 挂在 hold a banquet 后，而非再并列一个谓语；同理 向宾客敬酒致谢 处理为 propose a toast to thank the guests，“致谢”用 to thank 表目的。三个“拜”用 bow to A, to B and to each other 的并列介词 结构收紧，避免重复 bow 三遍。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 描述婚礼上惯常进行的仪式流程，回指全篇基调用一般现在时：bow / hold / propose 均用原形 （主语 the couple 视作复数，动词不加 s）。 并列结构平行 三个“拜”要保持平行：bow to Heaven and Earth, to their parents and to each other，介词 to 一致；几个主要动作 bow... hold... and propose... 也保持动词原形平行。 用词 “设宴”用 hold/give a banquet（a feast 亦可）；“敬酒”用 propose a toast / make toasts；“招 待宾客”用 entertain the guests；guests 用复数加 the 特指到场宾客。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: At the wedding, the couple bow to Heaven and Earth, to their parents and to each other, then hold a banquet to entertain the guests and propose a toast to thank them. 5. 今天，许多年轻人依然钟情于传统的中式婚礼，体验独特而美好的中国式浪漫。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 主干：年轻人 are fond of weddings（主语策略：原句主语） 主语明确是“许多年轻人”many young people。核心主干取 许多年轻人依然钟情于传统的中式婚 礼：many young people are still fond of / favor traditional Chinese weddings；体验独特而 美好的中国式浪漫 是钟情之下伴随发生的动作，降级处理。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 伴随动作降级为现在分词 体验独特而美好的中国式浪漫 是与“钟情”同时发生的伴随情形，降级为现在分词短语 experiencing the unique and wonderful Chinese-style romance 作伴随状语，挂在主干后，而 不是用 and they experience 另起一句。“独特而美好的”用并列形容词 unique and wonderful 前 置修饰 romance。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 “今天……依然钟情”讲当下的普遍现状，回指全篇基调用一般现在时 are fond of / favor；分词 experiencing 表伴随，时态随主句。 单复数与主谓一致 主语 many young people 复数，系动词用 are（are still fond of）；“传统的中式婚礼”泛指这一 类婚礼，用复数 traditional Chinese weddings 不加冠词。 搭配与用词 “钟情于”用 be fond of / be keen on / favor；“中国式浪漫”用 Chinese-style romance； romance 在此为不可数，不加复数、不加 a。
